name: Musée National Boubou Hama
subtitle: Sprawling 24-hectare open-air museum founded in 1959 featuring traditional pavilions, artisan workshops, and paleontology.

facts.label: Founded
facts.value: 1959 by Boubou Hama and Pablo Toucet

facts.label: Area
facts.value: 24 hectares overlooking the Niger River valley

facts.label: Highlights
facts.value: Sarcosuchus imperator dinosaur skeletons, traditional vernacular architecture, working artisan quarters, and botanical gardens

parts.text: The Musée National Boubou Hama is widely recognized as one of the most innovative and comprehensive museums in West Africa. Conceived as a living open-air cultural park where all strata of society could discover Nigerien heritage, it displays life-size replicas of Tuareg, Hausa, Zarma, and Songhai dwellings alongside dinosaur fossils discovered in the Tenere desert and active workshops of master weavers, leatherworkers, and silversmiths.
